primary_diagnosis_treated: Mixed diabetic‑hypertensive nephropathy (CKD stage 4) with hypertension and ischemic heart disease
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily (start low, titrate by 1.25 mg every 2–4 weeks to max 10 mg daily as tolerated)
medications.purpose: Control hypertension, reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 lists statin (e.g., atorvastatin 20 mg) for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily (titrate to target heart rate ~60 bpm as tolerated)
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of ischemic heart disease
medications.nice_justification: Standard IHD secondary‑prevention guidance; compatible with CKD and hypertension

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis (NG203 contraindicates metformin below this threshold)
Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention in stage 4 CKD (NG203 contraindicates chronic NSAID use)
eGFR 15.9 mL/min/1.73 m² is below the NICE TA775 threshold of ≥20 mL/min for initiation
Dual RAAS blockade increases risk of hyperkalaemia and AKI (NG203 contraindicates ACE‑I + ARB together)

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, liver function tests, and full blood count are required before starting Ramipril and Atorvastatin – assume they will be ordered.
Current blood pressure reading not provided; assume hypertension uncontrolled and target <130/80 mmHg given ACR >70 mg/g (NG203).
Allergy status to ACE‑I, statin, or beta‑blocker not documented – verify before prescribing.
Patient’s glucose‑lowering regimen not listed despite HbA1c 2.3 %; assume risk of hypoglycaemia and recommend review of diabetic medications.
treatment_summary: Start low‑dose Ramipril and titrate to control BP and reduce proteinuria, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg for lifelong cardiovascular protection, and add bisoprolol for ischemic heart disease secondary prevention. Avoid metformin, chronic NSAIDs, and SGLT2 inhibitors due to eGFR <30. Monitor potassium, creatinine, liver enzymes, and BP after initiation; review all agents annually and adjust doses as renal function changes.
